builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CAFE: Conducting-Cell-Aware Adaptive Differential Encoding for Robust DNN Inference in FeFET-Based Compute-in-Memory
summary: CAFE replaces two's-complement weight/activation encoding in FeFET-based compute-in-memory arrays with a selectively allocated differential encoding guided by a conducting-cell activity metric and NSGA-II search. The cost is 1.86-2.78x normalized array/encoding overhead plus a per-layer optimization and pruning pipeline, and accuracy still falls short of the ideal full-differential configuration in some layers. The method can fail if device variation statistics shift across chips or process conditions, invalidating the C2AM-guided allocation, and it presumes access to FeFET CIM hardware that the reader does not have.
rationale: The technique targets FeFET compute-in-memory hardware reliability, which is entirely outside the reader's GPU/API production inference stack and offers no adoptable artifact for that environment.
technique: Conducting-cell-aware differential encoding for FeFET CIM

claims.statement: CAFE replaces two's-complement weight/activation encoding in FeFET-based compute-in-memory arrays with a selectively allocated differential encoding guided by a conducting-cell activity metric and NSGA-II search. The cost is 1.86-2.78x normalized array/encoding overhead plus a per-layer optimization and pruning pipeline, and accuracy still falls short of the ideal full-differential configuration in some layers. The method can fail if device variation statistics shift across chips or process conditions, invalidating the C2AM-guided allocation, and it presumes access to FeFET CIM hardware that the reader does not have.

Reduces the proposed C2AM error metric by up to 28.6x; improves CIM inference accuracy by more than 87 percentage points over two's-complement encoding while approaching full-differential robustness at 1.86-2.78x normalized cost versus 3.06x for uniform full-differential encoding.
